A receita do subjuntivo: tire o «-o» e t: The subjunctive recipe: drop the «-o» and swap the vowel
PASSO 1: o subjuntivo é um conjunto de f: STEP 1: the subjunctive is a set of verb forms that Spanish uses after certain expressions, like «quiero que» or «es importante que». English has it too, but only as relics: "I suggest that he BE on time", "It's important that she GO", "God save the King", "Long live the Queen", "If I WERE you". In each case English uses an odd form ("be", "go", "save", "were") instead of the expected "is", "goes", "saves", "was". Spanish kept a full set of these forms and uses them every day, in ordinary conversation — not as something formal or old-fashioned. In this lesson you only learn to FORM them; the uses come in lessons 43 and 44. STEP 2: first, take the «yo» form of the present: «hablo», «como», «vivo». STEP 3: drop the final «-o»: «habl-», «com-», «viv-». STEP 4: add the SWAPPED vowel. -ar verbs switch to «e»: hable, hables, hable, hablemos, habléis, hablen. -er and -ir verbs switch to «a»: coma, comas, coma, comamos, comáis, coman; viva, vivas, viva, vivamos, viváis, vivan. STEP 5: to remember it: -ar verbs are the "a" verbs, so in the subjunctive they flip to «e»; -er and -ir verbs are the "e/i" verbs, so they flip to «a». STEP 6: the «yo» form is the same as the «él, ella, usted» form: «que yo hable» and «que él hable». When it could be confusing, use the pronoun. STEP 7: only the «vosotros» form has an accent: «habléis, comáis, viváis». In Latin America, «ustedes» is used instead: «hablen, coman, vivan». STEP 8: you've already used these forms in commands: the usted imperative and the negative tú imperative ARE subjunctive: «Hable más despacio», «No hables tan rápido», «Coma algo».
o português faz a mesma troca de vogal:: English has a subjunctive too, but only as fossils: "I suggest that he BE here", "It's essential that she ATTEND", "If I WERE you". Spanish uses its subjunctive all the time, in everyday speech. The good news: you already know some forms from the commands «Hable más despacio» and «No hables tan rápido» — that's the subjunctive.
Em -ar, a terminação de «tú» no subjunti: In -ar verbs, the «tú» ending in the subjunctive is «-es».
Em -ar, troque o «a» por «e» também em «: In -ar verbs, swap «a» for «e» in «vosotros» too.
Depois de «que» no subjuntivo, «yo» usa: English "I want YOU TO COME" can't be copied: when the subject changes, Spanish uses «que» + subjunctive.

Irregulares: a regra do «yo» e os seis r: Irregular verbs: the «yo» rule and the six rebels
PASSO 1: a regra do «yo» funciona para a: STEP 1: the «yo» rule works for most irregular verbs. If the «yo» form of the present is irregular, the subjunctive carries that irregularity into every person: tengo → tenga, tengas, tenga, tengamos, tengáis, tengan; hago → haga; digo → diga; vengo → venga; pongo → ponga; salgo → salga; traigo → traiga; oigo → oiga; veo → vea; conozco → conozca; conduzco → conduzca; caigo → caiga. STEP 2: stem-changing verbs (e → ie, o → ue) change in «yo, tú, él, ellos», but NOT in «nosotros» or «vosotros» — the same "boot" pattern as the present: pensar → piense, pienses, piense, pensemos, penséis, piensen; poder → pueda, puedas, pueda, podamos, podáis, puedan; querer → quiera, quieras, quiera, queramos, queráis, quieran. STEP 3: -ir verbs with a stem change ALSO change in «nosotros» and «vosotros»: dormir → duerma, duermas, duerma, durmamos, durmáis, duerman; sentir → sienta, sientas, sienta, sintamos, sintáis, sientan; pedir → pida, pidas, pida, pidamos, pidáis, pidan. STEP 4: six verbs have their own forms and are worth memorising (their «yo» doesn't end in «-o»: soy, estoy, voy, he, sé, doy): ser → sea; estar → esté; ir → vaya; haber → haya; saber → sepa; dar → dé. STEP 5: «esté» has an accent in every form except «estemos»: esté, estés, esté, estemos, estéis, estén. «Dé» has an accent only in the «yo» and «él» forms, to tell it apart from the preposition «de»: dé, des, dé, demos, deis, den. STEP 6: -uir verbs add «y» before the vowel: construir → construya, construyas…; «leer» is regular: lea, leas… STEP 7: a practical tip: when you meet a new verb, first ask yourself "what's the «yo» form?".
o português tem as mesmas irregularidade: The six rebels are exactly the verbs whose «yo» doesn't end in «-o» (soy, estoy, voy, he, sé, doy): sea, esté, vaya, haya, sepa, dé. For everything else, the «yo» form is your key: «tengo → tenga», «hago → haga», «digo → diga». English has nothing like this, so learn the six as a set.

Para manter o som: c/qu, g/gu, z/c e g/j: Keeping the sound: c/qu, g/gu, z/c and g/j
PASSO 1: no subjuntivo, a vogal final tr: STEP 1: in the subjunctive, the final vowel flips to «e» (in -ar) or «a» (in -er and -ir). That flip can change the sound of the consonant before it, so the spelling changes to keep the sound — the same idea as English "picnic → picnicking", where a «k» is added to keep the hard sound. STEP 2: -car verbs: «c» becomes «qu» before «e»: buscar → busque, busques, busque…; sacar → saque; tocar → toque. STEP 3: -gar verbs: «g» becomes «gu» before «e»: llegar → llegue; pagar → pague; apagar → apague. STEP 4: -zar verbs: «z» becomes «c» before «e» (Spanish rarely writes «ze»): empezar → empiece; cruzar → cruce; utilizar → utilice. STEP 5: -ger and -gir verbs: «g» becomes «j» before «a»: coger → coja, escoger → escoja, dirigir → dirija. STEP 6: «seguir» and «conseguir» lose the «u»: siga, consiga. «Jugar» changes both its stem and its spelling: juegue. STEP 7: the sound stays the same as in the infinitive: the «c» in «buscar» sounds like /k/, so in «busque» the «qu» keeps that sound. STEP 8: you already use these forms in commands: «Llegue temprano», «Busque aquí», «No llegues tarde».
o português faz exatamente o mesmo ajust: It's only spelling: the sound of the infinitive is kept. «buscar → busque» (/k/), «llegar → llegue» (hard /g/), «empezar → empiece» (Spanish avoids «ze»), «coger → coja» (the throaty /x/). English does something similar with "panic → panicked".
Antes de «e», o «g» /g/ precisa virar «g: Before «e», the hard /g/ «g» has to become «gu».
Antes de «e», o «z» vira «c», e o radica: Before «e», «z» becomes «c», and the stem changes to «ie».
Com «a», o «g» soaria /g/; para manter o: Before «a», «g» would sound hard /g/; to keep the /x/ sound, write «j».

— Bom dia, senhor Martínez. Entre e sent: — Good morning, Mr Martínez. Come in and have a seat, please.
